## My Thinking

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. I have about 10 mu. My husband goes to Shijiazhuang for construction work most of the year, so it's mainly me managing the fields, sometimes with help from my brother-in-law at harvest.

**What I will grow is obvious: winter wheat, then summer maize on the same land.** That is what we have always done. That is what my neighbors do. The soil here on the North China Plain is suited for it, and I know these two crops completely — when to water, when to apply fertilizer, what the plants should look like at each stage. I would not try something unfamiliar at my age with land I depend on.

**Wheat**: I will buy Jimai-series improved seed from the township cooperative, the same I used last year. It did well. I plant in mid-October after preparing the ground with the rotary tiller I rent from the village service station. I apply base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer plus urea — and topdress again in early spring when the plants green up. I irrigate before winter sets in, again in March, and once more at heading. That is three times. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually twice. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe more if spring rains cooperate.

**Maize**: Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid corn seed —郑单958 or similar, whatever the seed shop has in stock. I plant it quickly so it gets full growing season. I fertilize once at planting and topdress at the big bell stage. Rainfall in July and August usually handles most of the water, but if it is dry at silking I will pump once from the well. One spray for corn borer. Harvest in late September.

I keep maybe 1 mu near the house for garlic and vegetables for the household, but that is not really "farming" — it is just the garden.
